paragraphs.text: Or, “the Logos.” Gr., ho loʹgos; Lat., Verʹbum; J17,18,22(Heb.), had·Da·varʹ.
Lit., “was toward the God.” Gr., en pros ton The·onʹ; J17,18(Heb.), ha·yahʹ ʼeth ha·ʼElo·himʹ.
“A god.” Gr., the·osʹ, in contrast with ton The·onʹ, “the God,” in the same sentence; J17,18(Heb.), weʼ·lo·himʹ, “and god.” For a discussion of “a god,” see App 6A.
The punctuation of vss 3 and 4 is according to WH, Vgww and The Greek New Testament by the United Bible Societies.
“The only-begotten god,” P75אc; P66א*BC*, “only-begotten god”; ACcItVgSyc,h, “the only-begotten Son.”
“Elijah” (meaning “My God Is Jehovah”), J17,18,22; Gr., E·leiʹas.
Or, “I immerse; I dip.” Gr., ba·ptiʹzo.
That is, about 4 p.m., counting from sunrise.
Or, “the Anointed One.” Gr., ton Mes·siʹan; Lat., Mes·siʹam; J17,18,22(Heb.), ham·Ma·shiʹach.
“Cephas.” Gr., Ke·phasʹ. An Aram. name (Keh·phaʼ), here in the masc. gender, as in Mt 16:18 in Syr. mss. See Mt 16:18 ftn, “Rock-mass.”
Meaning “A Piece of Rock.” Gr., Peʹtros.
Or, “messengers.” Gr., ag·geʹlous; Lat., anʹge·los. Compare Job 33:23; Ps 91:11.
Lit., “What to me and to you?” meaning “What is there in common between me and you?” An idiom; a repellent question indicating objection. See App 7B.
Likely the bath that equaled 22 L (5.81 gal). See App 8A.
Or, “divine habitation (dwelling).” Gr., na·onʹ; Lat., temʹplum; J17,18,22(Heb.), ha·heh·khalʹ haz·zehʹ, “this palace (temple).”
“Is born again.” Lit., “should be generated from above.” Gr., gen·ne·theiʹ aʹno·then.
Or, “active force.” Gr., pneuʹma·tos; Lat., Spiʹri·tu; J17,22(Heb.), weha·ruʹach, “and the active force.” See Ge 1:2 ftn, “Force.”
“Heavenly things.” Gr., e·pou·raʹni·a; Lat., cae·leʹsti·a, “celestial things.”
“The world.” Gr., ton koʹsmon; Lat., munʹdum; J17,18,22(Heb.), ha·ʽoh·lamʹ.
That is, about 12 noon, counting from sunrise.
Lit., “A Spirit [is] the God.” Gr., Pneuʹma ho Theʹos.
That is, about 1 p.m., counting from sunrise.
“Bethzatha” (meaning “House of the Olive,” or, “House of Olives”), א; P75BVg, “Bethsaida,” meaning “House of Fishing”; ACSyc,hi,pArm, “Bethesda.”

P66,75אBDVgSyc omit vs 4; AItVgcSyhi,pArm add: “For an angel of the Lord [J9,22,23, “of Jehovah”] would come down into the pool from season to season and disturb the water; the first one then to step in after the disturbance of the water would become sound in health from whatever disease it was by which he was afflicted.”
Or, “in himself the gift of life.” See Ro 6:23.
“Resurrection of judgment.” Gr., a·naʹsta·sin kriʹse·os; Lat., re·sur·rec·ti·oʹnem iu·diʹci·i.
A denarius was a Roman silver coin that weighed 3.85 g (0.124 oz t).
Lit., “about twenty-five or thirty stadia.” A stadium equaled one eighth of a Roman mile, 185 m (606.75 English ft).
“In union with me.” Or, “in me.” Gr., en e·moiʹ.
Or, “is a devil.” Gr., di·aʹbo·losʹ e·stin.
Or, “Just what I have been saying to you.”
“You have seen Abraham?” P66ACDVg; P75א*Sys, “has Abraham seen you?”
“I have been.” For a discussion of Jesus’ prehuman existence, see App 6F.
“Siloam,” אAB; J7-14,16-19,22, “Shiloah.” See Isa 8:6 in LXX.
Or, “my life.” Gr., psy·khenʹ mou; J17,18,22(Heb.), naph·shiʹ. See App 4A.
Lit., “it is necessary [for] me to lead.”
“The festival of dedication (Hanukkah).” J22(Heb.), chagh ha·chanuk·kahʹ.
“What . . . things,” BItVg (אW, with a slight variation, agree); ASyh,p,s, “My Father, who has given me them, is greater than all others.”
Or, “at unity.” Lit., “one (thing).” Gr., hen, neuter, to show oneness in cooperation. See 17:21 and 1Co 3:8 ftns.
“You are gods.” Gr., the·oiʹ e·ste; Lat., diʹi eʹstis; J17,18,22(Heb.), ʼelo·himʹ ʼat·temʹ.
Lit., “about fifteen stadia away.” About 2.8 km (1.7 mi). A stadium equaled one eighth of a Roman mile, 185 m (606.75 English ft).
“I am the resurrection and the life.” Gr., E·goʹ ei·mi he a·naʹsta·sis kai he zo·eʹ; Lat., Eʹgo sum re·sur·recʹti·o et viʹta; J22(Heb.), ʼAniʹ hat·techi·yahʹ weha·chai·yimʹ.
About $260 with silver valued at $7 (U.S.) per oz t. See App 8A.
Or, “life.” Gr., psy·khenʹ; J17,18,22(Heb.), naph·shohʹ (from neʹphesh).
“Minister.” Gr., di·aʹko·nos; Lat., mi·niʹster (from miʹnus, “less”); J18,22(Heb.), mesha·rethiʹ, “my attendant.”
“One that is sent forth.” Or, “an apostle (envoy).” Gr., a·poʹsto·los; Lat., a·poʹsto·lus.
Or, “life.” Gr., psy·khenʹ; Lat., aʹni·mam; J17,18,22(Heb.), naph·shekhaʹ (from neʹphesh).
“Ask,” ADIt and in agreement with 15:16 and 16:23; P66אBWVgSyh,p, “ask me.”
Or, “another paraclete (comforter).” Gr., alʹlon pa·raʹkle·ton, masc.
Or, “the active force.” Gr., to pneuʹma, neuter. See Ge 1:2 ftn, “Force.”
“Beholds it . . . . You know it.” “It” (Gr., au·toʹ, neuter) refers to “the spirit” (to pneuʹma, neuter).
Or, “the paraclete (comforter).” Gr., ho . . . pa·raʹkle·tos, masc.
“That one,” masc., referring to the “helper,” masc.
Or, “the paraclete (comforter).” Gr., ho pa·raʹkle·tos, masc.
“That one,” masc., referring to the “helper,” masc. Compare 16:7.
“A sacred service.” Gr., la·treiʹan. Compare Ex 12:25 ftn.
Or, “the paraclete (comforter).” Gr., ho pa·raʹkle·tos, masc.
“Will give . . . convincing evidence.” Or, “will reprove.” Gr., e·legʹxei.
“That one,” masc., referring to “the helper,” masc., in vs 7.
“What he is talking about.” B omits.
Or, “in union with me.” Gr., en e·moiʹ. See 6:56 ftn.
Or, “their knowing you.” Gr., hiʹna gi·noʹsko·si se.
Or, “And I am holding myself sacred (treating myself as holy).” Gr., kai . . . e·goʹ ha·gi·aʹzo e·mau·tonʹ; Lat., et . . . eʹgo sanc·tiʹfi·co me ipʹsum; J17(Heb.), wehith·qad·dash·tiʹ.
Or, “at unity.” Lit., “one (thing).” Gr., hen, neuter, to show oneness in cooperation. See 10:30 ftn.
Lit., “before a throwing down [of seed].” Gr., pro ka·ta·bo·lesʹ.
Or, “the chiliarch.” Gr., ho khi·liʹar·khos; commander of 1,000 soldiers.
“King of the Jews.” Gr., ba·si·leusʹ ton I·ou·daiʹon; Lat., rex Iu·dae·oʹrum; J17,18,22(Heb.), meʹlekh hai·Yehu·dhimʹ.
“I should bear witness.” Gr., mar·ty·reʹso; Lat., te·sti·moʹni·um per·hiʹbe·am.
“What is truth?” Gr., Tiʹ e·stin a·leʹthei·a; Lat., Quid est veʹri·tas; J17,18(Heb.), Mah hiʼ ha·ʼemethʹ.

Or, “See! The man!” Gr., I·douʹ ho anʹthro·pos; Lat., ecʹce hoʹmo; J22(Heb.), Hin·nehʹ ha·ʼishʹ; J17(Heb.), Hin·nehʹ ha·ʼa·dhamʹ, “Look! The earthling man!”; J18(Heb.), Hin·nehʹ hag·ga·verʹ, “Look! The able-bodied man.” Compare Zec 6:12 ftn, “Man.”
Or, “Fasten [him] on a stake (pole)!” See App 5C.
“Authority.” Gr., e·xou·siʹan; Lat., po·te·staʹtem; J17(Heb.), reshuthʹ.
Or, “of the emperor.” Gr., tou Kaiʹsa·ros.
That is, about 12 noon, counting from sunrise.
Or, “he stopped breathing.” Lit., “he gave up the spirit.” Gr., pa·reʹdo·ken to pneuʹma.
“Pounds.” Gr., liʹtras, generally equated with the Roman pound that weighed 327 g (11.5 oz); Lat., liʹbras.
Lit., “about two hundred cubits.” See App 8A.
Lit., “I am having affection for you.” Gr., phi·loʹ se.
Lit., “I am having affection for you.” Gr., phi·loʹ se.
Lit., “are you having affection for me?” Gr., phi·leisʹ me.
Lit., “I am having affection for you.” Gr., phi·loʹ se.
Vs 25 is contained in אcABCVgSyp,s; א* omits.
